one_month_reasoning: The window runs to 2026-11-08, a Sunday, so the effective date is the Nov 6 close. Three scheduled events fall inside it. (1) The FOMC decision on Oct 28: Polymarket has no change at 83.5% and a 25bp hike at 16.5% ($32M volume). A hike helps Paycom's ~$105M of float income (FY26 guide) but raises discount rates on a stock that just re-rated, so I treat it as roughly neutral. (2) Q3 2026 earnings, expected Nov 4 after the close (Alpha Vantage calendar; Paycom has not confirmed the date). This is the dominant event. Over the last 12 reports the next-day move was -38.5%, -1.6%, -10.5%, +0.4%, +21.4%, +2.4%, +9.0%, +4.5%, -10.7%, +0.9%, +9.6%, +23.6% (Twelve Data daily closes): mean +0.9%, median absolute ~9%, RMS ~16% (~11% without the Nov 2023 guidance shock). The bar is now high. Q3 consensus EPS of $2.79 is +44% vs Q3'25's $1.94, with 19 of 19 revisions up, after the Q2 beat ($2.78 vs $2.38) and raise sent the stock up 23.6% in a day. The Q3 2025 print fell 10.7%. PEAD argues for slight upward drift after August's surprise, but the literature says the effect has weakened. (3) The October jobs report on Nov 6 (FRED). Payroll growth is weak, +29k in September and +46k/month on average since June, which matters for per-employee pricing. Net: a near-symmetric distribution around today's price with a slight positive median (+0.5% to +1%), a ~14% monthly sigma (above the 13% from annual vol / 3.5 because earnings sit inside the window), and a fatter left tail for a guidance disappointment.

fair_value.method: Blend of 60% P/E (17.0x Oct-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS of $15.02 = $255) and 40% DCF (FY27 FCF $665M growing 7%, 3% terminal, 9.5% WACC, net debt $785M, rolled forward 12 months = $268), giving ~$260.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct 2027 $15.02 (FY27 consensus $13.97, FY28 est. $15.37) x 17.0x (peer median 16.33x, range 9.0-23.0x)

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis consensus $13.97 (20 analysts); Alpha Vantage shows $13.95 with 20 up / 0 down revisions in 30 days.

13.97 x 1.10. ~10% growth = consensus revenue growth ~7.4% (src 10) plus modest margin gain (FY26 adj. EBITDA guide ~46% margin, src 1) and a lower share count (44.3M at 6/30/26 vs 54.8M at 12/31/25, src 1/3). That is below the 18.73% 3Y EPS growth forecast (src 9) because the 2026 buyback boost does not repeat.

Peer median forward P/E is 16.33x (range 9.0-23.0x, 10 peers). PAYC trades at 17.68x today (src 9), and its own forward P/E was 16.17x at FY2025 and 24.13x at FY2024 (src 11). 17x is inside the peer range, ~0.7 turn above the median; the premium rests on the highest margin in the set (Q2'26 adj. EBITDA margin 44.2%, src 1).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY27 FCF $665M (28% of $2.37B consensus revenue), +7%/yr to 2031, 3% terminal, WACC 9.5% (rf 5.22%, beta 0.89, ERP 4.23%, +0.86pp disruption premium), net debt $784.8M, 44.29M shares, +12-month roll-forward less $1.50 dividends

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2027 consensus revenue $2.37B (src 10) x 28% FCF margin. TTM FCF margin is 26.9% (575.1 / 2,140, src 9), and capex fell to $54.9M in H1'26 vs $270.9M in FY2025 (src 1, 3), so a ~1pt margin gain is reasonable.
Matches the consensus revenue growth forecasts: 7.44% for 2027 (src 10) and 7.67% 3Y CAGR (src 9).
Long-run nominal growth assumption, well below the 5.22% 10-year Treasury yield (src 31).

Ke = 5.22% rf (src 31) + 0.89 beta (Blume-adjusted 5Y beta 0.83, src 9) x 4.23% ERP (src 32) = 8.98%. Kd after tax = (4.00% FF upper bound, src 28, + 1.50% revolver margin, src 6) x 0.75 = 4.1%, at a 7% debt weight, so WACC = 8.64%. Added +0.86pp for the AI/seat-disruption risk the market priced in 2026: IGV fell 24% from Dec 2025 to Mar 2026 (src 24), and ADBE and INTU trade at 9.0x and 12.6x forward P/E (src 20, 18).
$982.8M debt less $198.0M cash (src 9); 44.3M shares outstanding at 6/30/26 (src 1).
EV = PV of 5 years of FCF + Gordon terminal value = $11.68B. Less $0.785B net debt gives $10.89B, or $245.9/share today. Rolled forward 12 months at 9.5%, less $1.50 of dividends: $268.

bear.story: The AI/seat-compression de-rating that hit software in H1 2026 returns (IGV -24% Dec-25 to Mar-26). Weak hiring (payrolls ~+30-50k/month) and a soft initial FY2027 guide (Feb 2027) of ~5-6% revenue growth follow. With the buyback authorization expired (Aug 15, 2026) and the revolver already $900M drawn, there is less buyback support. The multiple falls to ~11-12x NTM EPS of ~$14 (ADBE/INTU/BL territory): ~$165, still above the $126-135 average prices of the 2026 buybacks.

base.story: Revenue grows ~7-8% (in line with consensus), adj. EBITDA margin is ~46%+, and a lower share count lifts EPS to ~$15 NTM by Oct 2027. The multiple settles at the 16.3x peer median: ~$245. That is roughly flat to modestly up from $232 after an 85% rally off the June lows, consistent with the last 7 years of PAYC 12-month returns (median ~0).

bull.story: Automation and IWant/AI drive retention (91% in 2025) and price/attach. Revenue growth goes back to ~9-10%, the Fed hiking path (Polymarket: 2 hikes in 2026 at 71%) lifts float income, and capital return resumes with a new authorization. The multiple moves toward 20-21x (between the ADP/TYL top of the peer range and PAYC's FY2024 24x) on ~$15.5 NTM EPS: ~$315.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 9.02x (ADBE) to 23.00x (TYL); trailing EV/EBITDA 9.62x (ADBE) to 63.71x (NSP, depressed EBITDA), with a 13.2-18.8x core. No forward EV/EBITDA was available from a reachable source, so EV/EBITDA is trailing for every name, PAYC included.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: PAYC trades at 17.68x forward P/E and 15.06x trailing EV/EBITDA (both StockAnalysis). We use 17.0x NTM P/E: inside the range, ~0.7 turn above the 16.33x median, and below PAYC's own FY2024 (24.1x) and FY2023 (25.9x) forward multiples.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Only a small premium, which the margin structure supports. Paycom guides to a ~46% FY26 adj. EBITDA margin (Q2'26: 44.2%), the highest in the set. Recurring revenue is 95% of total, and the 3Y EPS growth forecast is 18.7% vs a ~12.3% peer median. I do not pay for the full EPS-growth gap: much of it comes from a one-off, debt-funded ~$1.4B buyback in H1 2026 (shares 54.8M to 44.3M), and revenue growth (7-8%) sits at the peer median, not above it. The premium therefore rests on margin, not growth, and stays well below the 2023-24 multiples.

thesis_break_reason: $150 is ~10.7x FY2027 consensus EPS ($13.97), below every high-quality peer except the AI-disruption-discounted ADBE/BL group, and ~35% below spot. It is also back inside the Feb-Jul 2026 trading range ($105-$150), when the market priced Paycom as a structurally ex-growth, AI-disrupted seat business. Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental break: an initial FY2027 guide at or below ~5% revenue growth, falling retention, or employment contraction cutting per-employee revenue. Ordinary volatility is less likely to explain it.

key_uncertainties: Whether the H1 2026 software de-rating (AI agents compressing seat-based HCM/SaaS demand) resumes. Peers ADBE/INTU/BL still trade at 9-13x forward EPS.
US employment: payroll growth is ~+30-50k/month and unemployment 4.2%. Per-employee-per-month pricing and new-logo sales are exposed to hiring slowing further.

Rate path: the 10-year at 5.22% and Fed hikes in 2026 lift float income but raise the discount rate. Client funds fell to $3.0B at 6/30 from $5.1B at year-end (seasonal), so the float sensitivity is seasonal.
Capital allocation after a ~$1.4B debt-funded buyback in H1 2026: the authorization expired Aug 15, 2026 and the revolver has $900M drawn. Will buybacks continue, and at what leverage?
Q3/Q4 2026 bar: consensus FY26 EPS of $12.10 implies an H2 of ~$6.17 vs H1's $5.93; estimates rose ~11% in 60 days, which raises the chance of a sell-the-news reaction.
Founder-CEO concentration and management changes: a new president in Feb 2026, and the former CFO and an early CIO added to the board in Jul 2026.
reasoning: Base rates first. PAYC's 139 overlapping 12-month windows since its 2014 IPO show a median log return of +24% (sd 0.42), but that history is dominated by the hyper-growth era. Over the last 7 years of start dates the median 12-month return is ~-1% (sd 0.39), with P(>+30%) 25% and P(<-30%) 24%. Three-year monthly realized vol is 47%, consistent with the 46% given. Conditioning on a >40% 6-month rally gives positive forward returns, but only from 2014-2020 samples, so I give it little weight. Valuation history: forward P/E has compressed from 78x (2021) and 26x (2023) to 16.2x at end-2025 and 17.7x now (StockAnalysis), around the 10-peer median of 16.3x. The stock is no longer cheap after an 85% rally from June's $125, but it is not stretched vs peers. Fundamentals (filings): Q2'26 revenue +9.8%, an adj. EBITDA margin of 44.2%, FY26 guidance raised to 7-8% revenue growth and a ~46% margin, and an aggressive H1 buyback of $1.39B (shares 54.8M to 44.3M), funded partly by a $900M revolver draw. Consensus EPS is $12.10 for FY26 and $13.97 for FY27, with revisions 20 up / 0 down. The sell-side average target ($220) sits below spot, typical lagging behaviour after a sharp re-rating. Macro and event odds: Polymarket puts US recession by end-2026 at only 6.5%, an October hold at 83.5% and two 2026 hikes at 71%; FRED shows unemployment 4.2%, weak payroll growth and a 10-year at 5.22%. Higher rates help float income but cap multiples. Fair value is $260 (P/E $255, DCF $268). The scenario-weighted value is ~$244 (bear $165/25%, base $245/50%, bull $315/25%). The 12-month ladder blends a lognormal centered at $240 with sigma 0.38 (below the 46% realized vol, which includes the 2026 crash-and-rebound regime) and the three-scenario mixture, giving P(>=232) ~0.56 and fatter left than right tails beyond ±40%. Research limits: WebSearch was unavailable (permission denied), so research ran through WebFetch on primary pages, the Twelve Data / Alpha Vantage APIs (several endpoints paywalled or rate-limited) and Polymarket's public API. No social or X sources were reachable without a search engine. Lane share: 25 of 35 sources are in-lane (price/valuation history, peer multiples documenting the 2026 sector re-rating, prediction markets, macro data, ERP, PEAD evidence, event timeline). Sources other lanes are unlikely to use: Polymarket Fed/recession markets, the FRED series, Damodaran ERP, and the computed earnings-reaction and 12-month return base rates.
